title: Yashpal v. State of U.P. — recovery citation; representation before Executive Engineer; Section 127 liberty
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shashi Kant Gupta, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; Executive Engineer to hear objections and pass a speaking final order; coercive recovery stayed; liberty to appeal under Section 127.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash a recovery citation of Rs. 10,20,135 was disposed of without examining the merits. The petitioner was directed to appear before the Executive Engineer with objections and evidence; the Engineer was to pass a speaking final order within four weeks. Coercive action was stayed for seven weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever earlier. If aggrieved by the final order, the petitioner could appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Non-appearance would revive the citation.
facts: Yashpal filed a writ in the Allahabad High Court seeking certiorari to quash a recovery citation dated 7 February 2020 issued by respondent no. 4 for Rs. 10,20,135. He alleged that the electricity department was taking coercive action without a hearing and without following the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition (Writ-C No. 6463 of 2020) was listed as fresh on 24 February 2020 and heard on 27 February 2020, when counsel for the petitioner and the electricity department were heard.

holding_units.topic: liberty to Section 127 appeal after speaking final order
holding_units.holding: Without deciding the validity of the recovery citation, the Court directed the petitioner to appear before the Executive Engineer with objections and evidence, required a speaking final order within four weeks, stayed coercive action for seven weeks or until disposal of the objection (whichever earlier), and reserved liberty, if the petitioner is aggrieved by that final order, to file an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 in accordance with law. Default in appearance would revive the citation.

principle_tags.application: The writ against the recovery citation was disposed of without a merits grant or refusal, with liberty to appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 if the petitioner is aggrieved by the Executive Engineer's final order.
The Court first required the Executive Engineer to pass a speaking final order on the petitioner's objections, and only thereafter reserved the Section 127 appeal against that final order.

not_decided.point: Validity of the recovery citation dated 7 February 2020 for Rs. 10,20,135
not_decided.note: The citation was neither quashed nor upheld; coercive action was only stayed pending the Executive Engineer's consideration.

not_decided.point: Whether the respondents followed the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Alleged in argument but not examined.
